summary: A hybrid of deckbuilding and worker placement where you send explorers around an island to unlock new action sites while your hand of cards funds resources and artifact purchases. Games feel like a satisfying puzzle of timing and resource conversion, with a low-conflict but competitively tense race for the best spots and cards.
praised: clever, tightly integrated fusion of deckbuilding and worker placement
satisfying exploration/discovery arc as new board sections open up
works well solo and scales cleanly across player counts
criticised: worker-placement blocking can feel harsh to players used to pure deckbuilders
heavy iconography takes a game or two to internalize
guardians and the research track add rules overhead for newcomers
some randomness in which cards/sites are available

interaction.kind: indirect blocking over shared worker-placement spots
interaction.detail: Players compete for the same limited action spaces and market cards, so taking a spot denies it to others that round, but each player's deck, resources, and exploration progress are entirely their own. There's no direct attack — interaction is about tempo and racing for the same opportunities.

scoring.how_you_win: Over five rounds you gather resources to explore, buy cards and defeat guardians; at the end all card values, research-track position and guardian tokens are totaled (with a penalty for hoarded resources), and the highest total wins.
